title: policy-eval-window-edge-silent-allow-leading-to-overage
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent silent-allow behavior observed at sliding-window boundaries for per-key and per-route rate policies. Some customers reported excess usage being accepted during tight bursts resulting in downstream billing reconciliation mismatches.

Observed behavior: For requests that arrive close to the end of a window boundary (sub-100ms), enforcement sometimes returns an allow while the accounting pipeline later attributes tokens to the previous window, producing an apparent double-count (billing shows tokens in both windows). This shows up as: 1) brief spike in accepted requests above configured burst caps, 2) billing/usage dashboards showing >100% of quota used in short periods, 3) some automated quota-based fallbacks not triggering.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed in reproduction): There are two coupled issues: (A) Window truncation mismatch: the policy evaluator uses millisecond-based fixed-window truncation when computing remaining credits, while the async metering aggregator canonicalizes timestamps to second granularity. At boundary edges this rounding difference can move a token count between windows. (B) Stale cached counters in the per-route in-memory cache are allowed to be served for up to 150ms to reduce RPCs; when combined with concurrent inflight evaluations the enforcer will permit requests based on a slightly stale low counter while the aggregator later attributes the same events to the prior window. Recent change in ENG-52211 (monotonic clock transition) exacerbated race by changing where we compute the canonical timestamp.

Why this is bad: causes customers to exceed configured limits without immediate throttling (unexpected capacity consumption), leads to billing reconciliation mismatches across the realtime meter and the offline billing pipeline, and can skirt quotas for short bursts that should have been blocked.

Reproduction steps:
1) Use org with strict per-route burst cap (e.g., route A: 100 req/min, burst 20).
2) Send burst that spans boundary: 10 requests at t=59.980s, 20 requests at t=60.010s, using concurrent clients to create ~40-60ms spread.
3) Observe enforcer logs: some accepts in the second group despite counters indicating cap exceeded.
4) Check metering output: events for the second group attributed to timestamp 59s (previous window) due to aggregator rounding.

Temporary mitigations (ship immediately):
- Lower cache TTL for per-route counters to 25ms for high-burst routes (config flag hotfix).
- Add emergency hard cap enforcement in gateway: if observed accept rate > 2x configured burst within 200ms, fallback to conservative deny.
- Add alert to billing dashboard for per-org >10% discrepancy between realtime enforcer counters and aggregator counts in 1m windows.

Proposed long-term fix:
1) Unify timestamp canonicalization across evaluator, aggregator, and billing pipeline: use the new monotonic_ns clock consistently in all modules and round to the same windowing granularity (decide on ms-level canonical windows).
2) Reduce in-memory cache staleness and change cache semantics to serve a conservative view (always bias toward lower available credits when TTL ambiguous).
3) Implement an eventual reconciliation job (daily) that compares shadow counters to billing aggregates and generates automatic correction entries and alerts for customer-facing discrepancies.
4) Add deterministic unit+integration tests that simulate high-concurrency boundary bursts (CI harness based on faker traffic driver).
5) Add dataplane canary rollout with shadow-mode enforcement (deny-only flagged) then full-enforce.

Acceptance criteria:
- No silent-allow events reproducible with the given harness for 10k simulated boundary bursts.
- Billing reconciliation discrepancy for canary customers reduced to <0.1% in 24h run.
- Hotfix for cache TTL applied and rolled back after fix is in.

Telemetry / Observability changes:
- New metric: rate_limit_boundary_mismatch.count (tags: org_id, route, policy_key).
- Dashboard panel: per-org real-time discrepancy (enforcer_count - aggregator_count) / aggregator_count.
- Log trace id to link enforcer decision with aggregator attribution for postmortems.

Risk and rollout: Low to medium code risk but high customer impact if delayed. Plan: patch runtime with unification and conservative cache policy, roll canary to 5% traffic for 48h, monitor metrics, then full rollout.

Notes: This ticket touches billing paths; coordinate with finance and billing team for reconciliation and customer communications. Also coordinate with ENG-53320 (metering-rewrite) which is scheduled in the same sprint to avoid merge conflicts.
